clue.text: Confused oriental world traveller taken in by plot

indicators.note: being taken in by something means being held inside it, so the plot word encloses the others

parts.note: a plot of ground in a garden is a bed
E is short for East, the oriental direction
Phileas Fogg travels round the world in Jules Verne's novel

explanation.surface: A traveller from the East, caught up in some scheme, has lost his bearings.
explanation.walkthrough: Phileas Fogg is the hero of Around the World in Eighty Days.
explanation.definitionFit: Befogged literally means wrapped in mist, so figuratively muddled or bewildered.

clue.text: In reserve, take part in secondary action

parts.note: something put by is saved in reserve
to play is to take part in a game

explanation.surface: Instructions to a substitute: wait in reserve, then join in a minor manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: Byplay is subsidiary action on stage, going on beside the main business.

clue.text: It's best to deliver direct

parts.note: first means top or best
to hand something over is to deliver it

explanation.surface: Advice that it is best to make a delivery in person.
explanation.definitionFit: Firsthand means directly from the source, without an intermediary.

clue.text: Malcontent with love for Marx

parts.note: a grouch is a grumbler or malcontent
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A disgruntled person who loves Karl Marx.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Karl; the answer is the comedian Marx brother.
explanation.definitionFit: Groucho was one of the Marx Brothers comedy team.

clue.text: Wipe before eating, for instance

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the word for before encloses the other

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
as is used to introduce an example, as in such as

explanation.surface: Advice to wipe your hands before a meal, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to rub out or wipe away.

clue.text: The sailor who left a mark?

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin

explanation.surface: A riddle asking which seaman left behind a mark.
explanation.walkthrough: A lascar is an East Indian sailor; 'who' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lascar was a seaman from India or Southeast Asia serving on European ships.

clue.text: Harp, perhaps carried by the 22

definitions.meaning: a stringed instrument played by the wind, the harp being one example
borne along by the wind, the answer to 22 down being a light wind

explanation.definitionFit: An Aeolian harp sounds when wind blows over its strings, and Aeolian deposits are those carried by wind, after Aeolus, god of winds.

clue.text: Old miners' leaders loaf around in the valley

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the loaf goes round the initials

parts.note: a cob is a round loaf of bread

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of the words Old and miners'

explanation.surface: Former mining chiefs idling about down in the valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A coomb is a short valley or hollow on a hillside, especially in southern England.

clue.text: Fugitives from war, say, with UN involvement

indicators.note: being involved, mixed up together, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Refugees from a conflict with the United Nations getting involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Runaways are people who have fled, so escapees or fugitives.

clue.text: Attempt to influence the modus operandi

definitions.meaning: to make overtures to someone, sounding them out
the method or way of tackling something

explanation.definitionFit: One may approach an official hoping to sway them, and an approach is a method of working.

clue.text: Poor Ron's one popular name for him, perhaps

indicators.note: poor here means badly made, signalling the letters are to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that poor Ron's one popular name for some man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges RONSONE, POPULAR and N together. 'Him' is an example of the grammatical item defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Him is a word standing in place of a noun for a particular person, i.e. a pronoun of that type.

clue.text: For example, an apprentice

definitions.meaning: the word an is one instance of the grammatical class of determiners like a and the
as a verb, to bind someone as a trainee under a formal agreement

explanation.definitionFit: An is the indefinite one of the grammatical determiners so called, and to article a clerk is to bind him as a trainee.

clue.text: Coloured archbishop heard expressing pain after a fall

parts.note: rain is a fall from the sky
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
the cry one hears from someone hurt is ow

explanation.surface: A colourful senior cleric cries out after tumbling over.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue word 'archbishop' must be split: 'Coloured arch' is the definition and 'bishop' gives B.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainbow is a coloured arc of light seen in the sky after a shower.

clue.text: King in a state!

parts.note: Carol was the name of two kings of Romania
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a monarch is in a dreadful state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' suggests agitation, but the parts are simply strung together.
explanation.definitionFit: Carolina names two US states, North and South.

clue.text: Opposed to putting, up house without pictures

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the house encloses the other piece
in a down clue, putting up means the word is set upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house
agin is dialect for against, opposed to

explanation.surface: Someone against erecting a house without any paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting up' reads the house backwards (IMES) in this down clue, and 'without' means outside. AGIN is dialect for against; 'pictures' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to see it in the mind, to envisage it.

clue.text: Offensive way to interrupt an Opposition statement

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle, so the way word goes inside the statement

parts.note: nay is a vote or statement of opposition
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: An MP's offensive interruption of the Opposition's statement in Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty and offensive are synonyms for something unpleasant or objectionable.

clue.text: The only one getting a record high score

parts.note: a single is a record with one track per side
a ton is a score of a hundred, as in cricket or darts

explanation.surface: The sole player to get both a hit record and a century.
explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is a solitary individual, one on its own.

clue.text: Exaggerated crisis, politically at the centre

parts.note: a drama is a crisis or exciting incident

indicators.note: the middle letters of the word politically are taken

explanation.surface: An overblown crisis at the heart of politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Dramatic behaviour is theatrical, overdone or exaggerated.

clue.text: A jockey's recommendation?

definitions.meaning: a jockey is one who rides a horse; the 's stands for is
a note added to a jury's verdict advising some course

explanation.definitionFit: A jockey is a horse rider, and a rider is also an addendum recommending something, as to a verdict.

clue.text: Allowances made in relationship with partners

parts.note: a ratio is a numerical relationship
North and South are partners in bridge

explanation.surface: Concessions made in a relationship between partners.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North and South play as a partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: Rations are fixed allowances of food or supplies.

clue.text: Old prince — the first to appreciate the heather?

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: taken as written
ling is a common name for heather

explanation.surface: An ancient prince was the first person to value heather.
explanation.walkthrough: An atheling was an Anglo-Saxon prince or nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Atheling was the Anglo-Saxon title for a royal prince or nobleman.

clue.text: Canine champion kept by ruler for sport

indicators.note: kept by means held inside, so the champion goes into the other letters
for sport means playfully, so the letters of ruler are jumbled

explanation.surface: A prize dog kept by a monarch for hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for sport' rearranges the ruler's letters to LURER. A lurcher is a crossbred hunting dog, often part greyhound, used by poachers.
explanation.definitionFit: A lurcher is a crossbred dog, typically part greyhound, used for hunting.

clue.text: A simple job for a cat's-paw

definitions.meaning: a light wind that ripples the surface of water

explanation.definitionFit: A breeze is slang for an easy task, and a cat's-paw is a light gust of wind.

clue.text: Great artists smear it indiscriminately

indicators.note: done without order or care, so the letters are scattered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Famous painters smearing paint around carelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestri is the Italian plural for masters, distinguished musicians or artists.

clue.text: College lecturer, not entirely of superior quality

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, so the letters sit inside it

explanation.surface: A college don who is not quite top-notch.
explanation.definitionFit: Elect as an adjective means choice or select, picked out as best.

clue.text: Town in America taking sides about a criminal

parts.note: burg is an American word for a town

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the sides go round the single letter

parts.note: L and R, left and right, are the two sides

explanation.surface: A US town choosing sides on a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A burglar is a criminal who breaks into buildings to steal.

clue.text: Depression makes a bachelor go astray

parts.note: to sin is to stray morally

explanation.surface: Gloom drives an unmarried man to wander off the straight path.
explanation.definitionFit: A basin is a hollow or depression in the land.

clue.text: Those in authority becoming better? What hopes!

indicators.note: becoming means turning into something else, so these letters change into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A sceptical jibe: our rulers getting better? Fat chance!
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for the establishment or ruling authorities.

clue.text: A joint in Paris is most attractive

parts.note: a joint of meat is a cut
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A Parisian restaurant or club is the prettiest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A joint in Paris' reads as a venue there, but 'in Paris' goes with 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutest is the superlative of cute, meaning prettiest or most appealing.

clue.text: Admission made by a player?

definitions.meaning: being let in, or the right to go in
an actor makes his arrival on stage

explanation.definitionFit: An entrance is both the right of access and an actor's arrival onstage.
